Day of appointment:
•	Greeter greets customer and puts appropriate advisor hat on hood of customer vehicle
•	Greet the customer at the car with a WOW intro, "I love this color."
•	Use the customer's name when greeting them, "Hello Mrs. Jones, welcome and I see you are coming in today for a check engine light."
•	Ask permission to get in car-tell them why-to retrieve the mileage-turn car on to get mileage and look for any indicator lights......all the while talking to the customer to build rapport "How is your day, how was your weekend, etc. Tell the customer what you are going to do, "WE are going to do a quick walkaround to check for any bumps & bruises and I am turning your wheel to check the tires." Do not ask them if they want to do this, command the customer. 
•	Check the tires & show the customer the tri-colored tire gauge EVEN IF IT IS GREEN.
•	Perform walkaroud, never turn your back on the customers, show tire specs and PET the DOG by finding common ground with the customer, "Oh, I see you are a Red Sox fan or I see your license plate in a specialized plate to help animals, or I see you have a membership fee to the gym, I go there too."
•	Plant seeds, "I see your tires are wearing unevenly, you might be due for an alignment."
•	Present at the desk 100% of the time "You are in for this service, but when I looked at your dash you are actually due for this service." "Before you came in today, I took the liberty of reviewing your history to be better prepared for your visit. I noticed last time you were here, we recommended an alignment, let's go ahead and get that done today." Notice that was NOT a question, but an assumptive close.
•	Review the history, show that you have done your homework all the while petting the dog.
•	Sell the MPI: We are going to perform a Multi-point health inspection (NOT can we or may we perform) and if the Tech "notices" (not finds) anything, I will let you know when I call to give you a status update.
•	Tell the customer when you will call for any update & how would they like to be contacted-text, email, phone call,
•	Close by presenting the CSI upfront (watch video).
•	Confirm transportation, waiting, etc.
•	If it is a drop off, advisor to make sure the customer is aware of the 1st time they will be contacted
Dispatch/Midday:
•	Vehicle is  then dispatched to a technician
•	MPI is to be completed in the 1st 15 mins if it is a waiter
•	Advisor reviews MPI, completes estimate and then is presented to the customer 
•	When you call with status regarding why their car is in the shop, you mention if the Tech has noticed anything from the MPI Health Inspection what they noticed "....and the total price is......and we have the parts in stock and can complete this work by our promise time..." and shut up.
•	Remind them of CSI "Remember I mention the survey this morning, how am I doing so far on your visit?"
ACTIVE DELIVERY:
•	Once vehicle is complete, vehicle is then washed, vacuumed, number tag is pulled from mirror and plastic seat cover is removed
•	SET THE APPOINTMENT FOR THE PICK UP: Greet them just like in the AM. Perform an active delivery over the phone (if customer is waiting perform in person) Set up a pick up time 
•	Customer arrives at dealership and then the active delivery process is initiated
•	Advisor is to go over work performed line by line
•	MPI is gone over and signed
•	Final paper work is then signed
•	Tommy Card rewards are explained
•	Set next service Appointment 
•	Remind them of CSI for the 3rd time and walk them to the car, thank them for business.
•	Customer is then walked to their vehicle by the advisor and we thank them for their business
Follow up:
•	Service Advisor to call customers after 24hrs
•	Advisor to go over service that was done to see if there are any questions r issues 
•	If customer is happy thank them for service and remind them about survey 
•	If customer is unhappy try to resolve issue if unable to get Service Manager involved 
•	Document call thru vin solutions

Appointment:
	•	Customer calls or makes an appointment online
Ensure the customer is aware of the CONES so they know where to go,
•	Explain the service drive process and what is going to happen the day of the appointment 
•	Ensure they know WHO will be helping them,
•	Confirm transportation,
•	Off the phone, check on and SOP's needed for appointment.

Regarding the pre-writes:
•	What was recommended in the past & declined,
•	What should have been recommended in the past & was neglected,
•	What is needed at this visit,
•	Any repeat concerns to follow up on,
•	Any recalls/campaigns,
•	Any SOP's.
Day of appointment:
•	Greeter greets customer and puts appropriate advisor hat on hood of customer vehicle
•	Greet the customer at the car with a WOW intro, "I love this color."
•	Use the customer's name when greeting them, "Hello Mrs. Jones, welcome and I see you are coming in today for a check engine light."
•	Ask permission to get in car-tell them why-to retrieve the mileage-turn car on to get mileage and look for any indicator lights......all the while talking to the customer to build rapport "How is your day, how was your weekend, etc. Tell the customer what you are going to do, "WE are going to do a quick walkaround to check for any bumps & bruises and I am turning your wheel to check the tires." Do not ask them if they want to do this, command the customer. 
•	Check the tires & show the customer the tri-colored tire gauge EVEN IF IT IS GREEN.
•	Perform walkaroud, never turn your back on the customers, show tire specs and PET the DOG by finding common ground with the customer, "Oh, I see you are a Red Sox fan or I see your license plate in a specialized plate to help animals, or I see you have a membership fee to the gym, I go there too."
•	Plant seeds, "I see your tires are wearing unevenly, you might be due for an alignment."
•	Present at the desk 100% of the time "You are in for this service, but when I looked at your dash you are actually due for this service." "Before you came in today, I took the liberty of reviewing your history to be better prepared for your visit. I noticed last time you were here, we recommended an alignment, let's go ahead and get that done today." Notice that was NOT a question, but an assumptive close.
•	Review the history, show that you have done your homework all the while petting the dog.
•	Sell the MPI: We are going to perform a Multi-point health inspection (NOT can we or may we perform) and if the Tech "notices" (not finds) anything, I will let you know when I call to give you a status update.
•	Tell the customer when you will call for any update & how would they like to be contacted-text, email, phone call,
•	Close by presenting the CSI upfront (watch video).
•	Confirm transportation, waiting, etc.
•	If it is a drop off, advisor to make sure the customer is aware of the 1st time they will be contacted
Dispatch/Midday:
•	Vehicle is  then dispatched to a technician
•	MPI is to be completed in the 1st 15 mins if it is a waiter
•	Advisor reviews MPI, completes estimate and then is presented to the customer 
•	When you call with status regarding why their car is in the shop, you mention if the Tech has noticed anything from the MPI Health Inspection what they noticed "....and the total price is......and we have the parts in stock and can complete this work by our promise time..." and shut up.
•	Remind them of CSI "Remember I mention the survey this morning, how am I doing so far on your visit?"
ACTIVE DELIVERY:
•	Once vehicle is complete, vehicle is then washed, vacuumed, number tag is pulled from mirror and plastic seat cover is removed
•	SET THE APPOINTMENT FOR THE PICK UP: Greet them just like in the AM. Perform an active delivery over the phone (if customer is waiting perform in person) Set up a pick up time 
•	Customer arrives at dealership and then the active delivery process is initiated
•	Advisor is to go over work performed line by line
•	MPI is gone over and signed
•	Final paper work is then signed
•	Tommy Card rewards are explained
•	Set next service Appointment 
•	Remind them of CSI for the 3rd time and walk them to the car, thank them for business.
•	Customer is then walked to their vehicle by the advisor and we thank them for their business
Follow up:
•	Service Advisor to call customers after 24hrs
•	Advisor to go over service that was done to see if there are any questions r issues 
•	If customer is happy thank them for service and remind them about survey 
•	If customer is unhappy try to resolve issue if unable to get Service Manager involved 
•	Document call thru vin solutions

•	MPI is gone over and signed
•	Final paper work is then signed
